notes:
Account snapshot: mid-market product analytics company building a contextual help + in-app search product. Started on Redwood hosted API for fast prototyping; after positive latency/cost results, asked to evaluate Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation.

POC summary: hosted trial showed ~95ms median, p95 180ms for chat endpoints with 1k token prompts (avg). Cost via hosted API projected ~$0.12/token-unit at current profile (approx). POC for Dedicated ran on a small reserved pool (2 x A10g-equivalent nodes) for 2 weeks: throughput improved 2.6x at 8 concurrent workers, observed KV cache hit ~18% after warm-up.

Requirements from Polaris product/infra:
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms for chat support flows (target 150ms)
- Throughput: steady-state 30-45 rps during peak; burst to 120 rps for product launches
- Cost: looking to move unit economics to <$0.08/token-unit at scale; sensitive to overage multipliers
- Security: VPC peering, SSO (SAML), KMS integration, SOC2 evidence, data residency for NA region

Pricing / packaging negotiation highlights:
- Polaris asks for 12-month Dedicated commitment with a 3-stage ramp (Q1: 25%, Q2: 60%, Q3+: 100% of committed vGPU hrs).
- Proposed Redwood offer: 9-month ramp, base commit 400 vGPU-hours/month (equiv.) with 2x burst buffer (burst billed at 1.2x up to 50% of commit in a month) and overage at 1.5x after burst buffer.
- Polaris counters: wants 2.0x burst at 1.0x price for first 2 months of a launch window and overage capped at 1.25x for first year.
- Finance sensitivity: requires predictable monthly cap during pilots; requesting a capped overage escrow or true-up mechanism to avoid surprise bills.
- SE notes: possible to offer an initial 3-month pilot commit discount (20%) then standard rates; can instrument token-level telemetry for billback to product teams.

Legal / procurement notes:
- Procurement asked for an MSA with standard carveouts; R&D wants a data processing addendum that clarifies KV cache retention and deletion windows.
- Security asked for pen-test attestation and a short SOC2 extract; we pointed them to Redwood security FAQ (drive link).

Recent feedback from product VP (L. Carter): "If we can lock in predictable unit cost and a reasonable burst policy for launches, Dedicated is a no-brainer. Biggest risk is billing surprises during marketing spikes."

Next steps (short):
- Evan to deliver final pricing spreadsheet with 3 commitment scenarios (base: 400 vGPU-hrs, mid: 800 vGPU-hrs, high: 1400 vGPU-hrs) by 2026-02-18.
- SE (Priya) to prepare a technical runbook that maps their peak profile to commit/burst settings and expected p95 improvements by 2026-02-17.
- Legal to receive redlined MSA by Polaris on 2026-02-21; procurement follow-up call week of 2026-02-24.
- Finance/operations to discuss capped overage proposal (internal) — blocker until we present numbers.
